what: An orders list: a sidebar pinned corner to corner holding an avatar and two nav buttons, a heading, a 2px divider, four identical stacked rows, and a declared table placeholder.
why: Guards the structural rules that depend on measurement rather than on style — the sidebar span rule, the divider thinness trigger, and the list-item set rule that needs three or more identical stacked boxes before any of them reads as a row.
notes: The 5 inferred are the avatar (a small filled circle) and the four rows. list-item? is the expected reading: the set is recognised, but membership of a set is a guess rather than a structural certainty.
If a change ever makes the four rows read as `card` or `shape`, the set rule has broken — that is the regression this fixture exists to catch.
The sidebar is 798px tall inside an 800px frame. Shortening it materially should make it read as a card; that is the span rule, and it is deliberate.
